Employee'S Compensation Act, 1923, Against The
Judgment And Award Dt.26.11.2020 Passed In Eca

 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the petitioner under Section 30(1) of the Employee's Compensation Act,
1923 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the E.C. Act"), being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge & Commissioner for Employee's Compensation, Kundapura (hereinafter for brevity referred NC: 2024:KHC:20852 to as "the Commissioner"), dated 26.11.2020 in E.C.A.No.08/2016, granting compensation of a sum of `2,31,688/- with interest at 12% per annum from 18.03.2016, on the ground that the compensation awarded is on the lower side and requires enhancement.
2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 (Insurer).
Respondent No.1, who was placed ex- parte before the Commissioner has remained un- represented in spite of service of notice upon him in this Court also.
3. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties before the Commissioner is retained.

4. The case of the claimant who was the petitioner in the Commissioner is that, he filed a claim petition under Sections 8 and 10 of the E.C. Act, claiming compensation of a sum of `10,00,000/-
with interest from the respondents, on account of the injuries sustained by him during the course of his employment under respondent NC: 2024:KHC:20852 No.1, as a driver of the Autorickshaw Sri Sandesh vs Sri Raghavendra on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158075953/
2 bearing registration No.KA-20/C-2102.
5.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case of the petitioner before the Commissioner is that, he was working as a driver of the Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-20/C-2102, belonging to the first respondent.

When he was driving the said Autorickshaw on 18.03.2016, at about 8:30 p.m., during the course of his employment, he met with an accident near Gopadi Temple, on NH-66, Kundapura Taluk, since two dogs suddenly crossed the road and dashed to the said Autorickshaw.
Due to the said accident, the Autorickshaw was damaged and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Chinmayi Hospital, Kundapura, where he was treated as an in-patient.
He underwent several surgeries for his fracture injuries.
It is stated that the petitioner has spent more than a sum of `1,50,000/- towards his treatment.

He has suffered permanent disability due to the accidental injuries NC: 2024:KHC:20852 and is not in a position to do any work and is also unable to continue his avocation of driving the vehicles in future.
Due to the accidental injuries, his family members are suffering great hardship and loss.
Therefore, he prayed to award reasonable compensation for the accidental injuries sustained by him during the course of his employment.
6. In response to the notices served upon the respondents before the Commissioner, since the first respondent remained absent and un-represented, he was placed ex-parte.
However, the second respondent-Insurer appeared before the Commissioner and filed its Written Statement.
In its Written Statement, it denied the averments made in the petition as false.

It contended that there was no relationship of employer and employee between the respondent No.1 and the petitioner and that the petitioner was not driving the Autorickshaw belonging to the first respondent.

Though the respondent No.2 - insurer admitted the issuance of insurance policy in NC: 2024:KHC:20852 respect of the Autorickshaw in question, but contended that its liability would be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
With the said contentions, it prayed to reject the petition with cost.
7. Based upon the pleadings of the parties, the Commissioner framed the following issues for its consideration.
1. Whether the petitioner proves the alleged relationship of employer and employee between the respondent No.1 and the petitioner as on 18-03-2016?

2. Whether the petitioner proves that on 18-03-2016 at about 08-30 p.m., while the petitioner was driving an auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-20-C-2102 belonging to the respondent No.1 (i.e.
during the course of duty as an employee under the respondent No.1) met with an accident near Gopadi Temple, on NH-66, Kundapura Taluk and suffered the alleged injuries?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief claimed?
what is the just and reasonable compensation to which the petitioner is entitled?
from which of the respondents, the petitioner is NC: 2024:KHC:20852 entitled for the compensation?
what is the rate of interest?

8. In order to prove his case, the claimant/petitioner (appellant herein) got himself examined as PW-1 and examined two more witnesses, i.e. one Sri. Raghavendra, the owner of the Autorickshaw as PW-2 (employer) and the treated Doctor at Chinmayi Hospital, Dr. Dinesh Kumar Shetty as PW-3 and got marked as many as 39 documents from Exs.P-1 to P-39, which included the complaint, personal documents like Aadhaar card, driving licence, etc., and hospital records,
medical bills and x-rays.
On behalf of the second respondent-Insurer, though no witness was examined, however, a copy of the insurance policy was got marked as Ex.R-1 and cross-examined the witnesses.

9. After hearing the arguments of the parties and going through the entire material placed before it,
the Commissioner, by answering issues No.1 and 2 in the NC: 2024:KHC:20852 affirmative, issue No.3 partly in the affirmative, and issue No.4, as per the final order, allowed the claim petition in part by granting compensation of a sum of `2,31,688/-
with interest @12% per annum from the date of the claim petition until its realisation and fixed the liability upon the respondent No.2 - Insurer to deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest within 30 days from the date of the said order.

It details of compensation are as follows:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in ` 1 Loss of earning capapcity caused 2,18,794-00 by the injuries/disability 2 Reimbursement of medical 12,894-00 expenses Total 2,31,688-00
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, on the ground that it is on the lower side, the petitioner has filed this appeal, seeking enhancement of compensation.

10. Learned counsel for the petitioner strenuously contended that the Commissioner grossly erred in re- NC: 2024:KHC:20852 assessing the permanent disability of the petitioner at 18% to the whole body,
when in fact, the entire permanent disability of 36% as assessed by the Doctor was required to be taken into consideration as stipulated under the provisions of Section 4(1) of the Schedule of the E.C. Act.
Thus, he prayed to enhance the compensation by modifying the impugned judgment and award passed by the Commissioner.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the second respondent - Insurer supported the award passed by the Commissioner.
12. This Court admitted the appeal on 01.02.2022, however, without framing the substantial question of law.

However, today, the substantial question of law is framed as under:
" Whether the Commissioner is justified in taking the disability of 18% to the whole body though Section 4(1) of the E.C.Act contemplates to take the entire disability as assessed by the Doctor?"

4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 13.

The above substantial question of law framed by this Court is answered in the negative for the following reasons:
13.

On the basis of the evidence on record, the learned counsel for the petitioner specifically contended that as per the evidence of PW-3 - Dr. Dinesh Kumar Shetty,
an Orthopedic surgeon, who treated the patient (petitioner) when he was admitted in Chinmayi Hospital immediately after the accident has deposed specifically that it was he who treated the petitioner when he was admitted to the said Hospital.
He stated that the petitioner took treatment as an in-patient and he was operated and implants were fixed.
He stated that after the discharge, the petitioner took follow-up treatment as an out-patient for nearly seventeen times.
Further the Doctor (PW-3) has specifically deposed that the petitioner has sustained injuries on his left leg but by mistake, in the Wound Certificate, it is mentioned as right leg.

He further deposed that when he examined the petitioner on - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 21.09.2018, he noticed that there was mal-union of fractured bones and also noticed that there was varus deformity of left ankle 10 degree, puckard scar medial aspect, DF/PF arc reduced by 90%, inversion Eversion reduced by 60%, reduced sensation over dorsum of foot.
He opined that the petitioner may have difficulty in walking on uneven surface, brisk walk, squatting down, climbing up and down the stairs, etc.

Thus, considering the nature of injuries, operation undergone and the deformity and difficulty faced by the petitioner, he opined that the petitioner suffered the permanent partial total disability of 36% in his left lower limb.
Further, he deposed that the petitioner needs removal of implants, the cost of which would be around `20,000/-.

In support of his deposition, the discharge summary at Ex.P-30 shows that the petitioner has sustained laceration 12x10 cm. antero medial aspect of left ankle, 10x6 cm. distal 1/3 tibia exposed, dislocation of ankle with total tear of deltoid ligament dorsalis pedis vessels and open fracture medial and lateral malleolus.

Ex.P-30 further reveals that the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 petitioner was treated by Emergency wound debridement, repair of deltoid ligament, ORIF medial malleous with K-wire and ORIF Febula with LCP.

It further shows that the petitioner was discharged on 28.03.2016 and on the same day, due to increased pain and infection,
he was re-admitted and discharged on 03.04.2016.
Thereafter he has taken treatment as an out-patient for seventeen times.

Thereafter on 21.09.2018, the Doctor has once again examined the petitioner and found the following problems:

sentences.text: It also mentions - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 that the petitioner needs removal of implants, the cost of which would be around `20,000/- towards future medical expenses.
14. During cross-examination of PW-3 (Doctor), this witness stated that he cannot say that the petitioner cannot pursue his avocation of driving at all.
He further stated that he cannot say that the disability assessed by him when compared to the whole body would be half of it.

Merely because this witness has stated that he cannot say that the disability assessed by him when compared to the whole body would be 50%, the disability assessed by him cannot be accepted for the reason that as per Section 4(1) of the E.C. Act, whatever disability assessed by the Doctor towards a particular organ shall be considered as the disability and cannot be considered or compared to the whole body as considered by the MACTs in the Motor Vehicle Accident cases.

15. For convenience, the provisions of Section 4(1)(c)(ii) of the E.C. Act is extracted below:
- 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 4. Amount of Compensation .-(1)

Subject to the provisions of this Act, the amount of compensation shall be as follows, namely:
(a)xxx xxx xxx (b)xxx xxx xxx (c) where permanent partial disablement result from the injury (i) xxx xxx xxx (ii) in the case of an injury not specified in Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity (as assessed by the qualified medical practitioner)
permanently caused by the injury;
Sri Sandesh vs Sri Raghavendra on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158075953/
6 16.

entities.text: Sri Sandesh vs Sri Raghavendra on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A careful reading of the provision 4(1)(c)(ii) of the E.C. Act clearly stipulates that, in case the injury is not specified in Schedule 1, then, such percentage of the compensation payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 capacity as assessed by the qualified medical practitioner
is required to be taken.

17. In the instant case, as per the evidence of the Doctor (PW-3) and the documentary evidence, i.e.
discharge summary at Ex.P-30, the petitioner was suffering from partial permanent disability of 36% towards left lower limb.

When such being the case, the contention of the learned counsel for the second respondent - Insurer that, 50% of the disability assessed by Doctor must be taken (i.e.18%)
as the disability, cannot be accepted.

The Commissioner, while considering the disability has slipped into an error by considering 50% of the disability assessed by the Doctor, at 18% (36%/2), which is in gross violation of the provisions of Section 4(1) of the E.C. Act.

Therefore, the same is liable to be rectified and the impugned award is liable to be modified as under:
18.

The petitioner has stated that he was getting salary of a sum of `10,000/- per month from the respondent No.1 (employer) and also a sum `100/- per - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 day as batta, but he has not produced any documentary evidence.

The Central Government, vide relevant notification issued by the Ministry of Labour Employment dated 31.05.2010, for the purpose of employees Compensation Act, had fixed the monthly wages at `8,000/-.

However, considering the oral evidence of the petitioner as well as the employer (PW-2),
the Commissioner held that, it is settled proposition of law that when the income is pleaded and proved, the same is to be considered.
Accordingly, he assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at `11,000/- [i.e. `8,000/- + `3,000/- (`100 per day x 30 days)].
The said assessment of income is just and proper and the same is retained.

19. As per Section 4(1) of the E.C. Act, the amount of compensation shall be an amount equal to 60%
of the monthly wages of the injured employee, multiplied by the relevant factor and also multiplied by the percentage of disability.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, i.e. Driving Licence at Ex.P-4, the Commissioner has assessed the age of the injured petitioner as 40 years, for which the factor applicable is 184.17,
which is not disputed.
The same being just and proper, I retain the same.

7 21.

sentences.text: Accordingly, 60% of `11,000/- comes to `6,600/-.

Thus adopting relevant factor of 184.17 and disability at 36%, the loss of earning capacity caused by the injuries/disability works out to `4,37,587.92 (i.e. `6,600/-x184.17x36%) as against `2,18,794/- awarded by the Commissioner.
22. Further, towards medical expenses, the Commissioner has awarded a sum of `12,894/-.
The petitioner has produced 21 medical bills from Exs.P-6 to P- 26.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence coupled with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, duration of treatment undergone, follow-up treatments, surgeries undergone etc., the compensation - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 awarded towards medical expenses at `12,894/- is just and proper and the same is retained.

23. Thus the petitioner is entitled to the modified compensation as below:
Sl

. No . Head of Compensation Amount in ` 1 Loss of earning capacity caused 4,37,587-92 by the injuries/disability (i.e. `6,600/-x184.17x36%) 2 Reimbursement of medical 12,894-00 expenses Total 4,50,481-92 24.
Thus, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Commissioner at `2,31,688/- is enhanced to a sum of `4,50,481-92, rounded off to `4,51,000/-.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the petitioner (appellant herein) stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge &
Commissioner - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:20852 for Employee's Compensation, Kundapura, dated 26.11.2020 passed in ECA No.08/2016, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `2,31,688/- is enhanced to a sum of `4,51,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Fifty One Thousand only), with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation.
The second respondent - Insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation by adjusting if any compensation already deposited with interest at 12% per annum, within sixty days from the date of receipt of a copy of the award;

Out of the enhanced compensation of a sum of `2,19,312/-, 50% of the said sum shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner, in any Nationalised Bank, for a period of five years with permission to withdraw the periodical interest.
- 20 -  NC: 2024:KHC:20852  Remaining 50% of the enhanced compensation shall be released in favour of the petitioner, after his proper identification, in accordance with law.
Draw the modified award accordingly.
